chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a mutamattiʿ who fasted three days during the hajj, then obtained a sacrificial animal on the day he departed from Minā. He said: His fasting suffices him.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him and fulfilled the obligation
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the three days of fasting required in this context
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the ritual site associated with hajj rites
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial animal offered in hajj

ai.seo_question: If a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ fasts three days instead of offering hady and then finds an animal later, is the fasting still sufficient?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the mutamattiʿ in hajj who was unable to offer the hady and therefore fasted three days. If he later obtains a sacrificial animal on the day he leaves Minā, his completed fasting is sufficient and remains valid.
